name: Files.com
description: Store files, manage folders, automate transfers, and orchestrate secure file operations.

authentication.name: Files.com Header API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Files.com API key sent only in the X-FilesAPI-Key header. Files.com API keys inherit the owning user's permissions.

credentials.name: Site URL
credentials.description: Full Files.com site URL, for example https://your-subdomain.files.com. Do not include /api/rest/v1.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: Files.com API key to send in the X-FilesAPI-Key header. This key inherits the owning user's permissions; admin actions need a site-admin service user.

setupGuide.title: Connect Files.com Header API Key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Files.com account with permission to create API keys. Files.com does not use OAuth scopes here; the API key inherits the owning user's permissions, so use a site-admin service user when you want admin actions such as Users, Groups, Permissions, Workspaces, Site Settings, Syncs, Automations, or audit history.

steps.title: Create or copy a Files.com API key
steps.description: In Files.com, open API Keys and create a key with the permissions you want MindCloud to use. Copy the API key value.

steps.title: Enter your Files.com site URL
steps.description: Enter your full Files.com site URL, for example https://mindcloud3.files.com. Do not add /api/rest/v1.

steps.title: Paste the API key
steps.description: Paste the API key into the API Key field. MindCloud sends it only in the X-FilesAPI-Key header for this auth type.

actions.name: Upload File
actions.description: Creates a new file in Filestage from a URL.

arguments.name: Step Ids
arguments.description: Array of step IDs. This is only required if the `projectId` is empty

arguments.name: Project Id
arguments.description: The ID of the project to upload the file to. This field is required when the `stepIds` field is empty

arguments.name: File Id
arguments.description: The ID of the file that gets new version.

arguments.name: File URL
arguments.description: A URL where the file can be downloaded. Our server will perform a GET request to this URL.

arguments.name: File Headers
arguments.description: A key-value map of HTTP headers to include in the GET request to the `fileURL`. You can use this to provide authentication tokens (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) if the URL is protected or other headers neccessary to make the GET request to the `fileUrl` successful.

arguments.name: Callback URL
arguments.description: The URL where we will send a POST request to notify you of the upload's final status. This URL must be publicly accessible.

arguments.name: Callback Headers
arguments.description: A key-value map of HTTP headers to include in the POST request to your `callbackURL`. Use this for security, such as including a pre-shared secret or auth token.

arguments.name: File Name
arguments.description: The desired name for the file, including its extension (e.g., `document.pdf`). If omitted, the name will be inferred.

arguments.name: Uploader Email
arguments.description: The email address of the user you want to upload the file on behalf of. This user will be displayed as the file uploader.

arguments.name: Section Id
arguments.description: The ID of a specific section within a project to organize the file into. If omitted, the file is placed in the default section.

arguments.name: Pregenerated File Id
arguments.description: `pregeneratedFileId` in the response body of `POST /files/upload-url`

arguments.name: External Id
arguments.description: A custom identifier from your system to associate with the file, useful for cross-referencing. **Note:** We do not enforce uniqueness on this field; it is your responsibility to manage it.

arguments.name: External Metadata
arguments.description: Custom data that could be associated with the File. `externalMetadata` field cannot exceed 10Kb of data size and also a maximum of 5 object properties are allowed in this object.

authentication.description: Use your Finmo access key as username and secret key as password.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Finmo account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Finmo sandbox or production account and an Access API key + Secret API key pair from the Finmo dashboard.

steps.title: Open the Finmo Dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to your Finmo dashboard so you can manage API keys for this account.

steps.title: Create or reveal an API key pair
steps.description: Generate or open an Access API key and Secret API key pair in Finmo. Finmo generates these keys together.

steps.title: Copy both keys somewhere secure
steps.description: Keep the Access API key and Secret API key together. If you rotate the pair later, update this connection with the new pair.

steps.title: Enter the Finmo keys in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the Access API key into the username field and the Secret API key into the password field.

authentication.description: Use a Google service account to sign a JWT assertion and exchange it for an OAuth2 access token.
authentication.notes: Google service-account auth is an OAuth2 JWT bearer token exchange. MindCloud currently represents this as custom auth because the OAuth2 auth editor is built around authorization-code and client-credentials flows, not signed JWT assertions.

setupGuide.title: Connect Firebase with a Google service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Google Cloud service account key with access to the Firebase projects you want to manage.

steps.title: Create or select a Google Cloud service account
steps.description: In Google Cloud, use a service account that has permission to access the Firebase Management API for the target projects.

steps.title: Create a JSON key
steps.description: Open the service account, create a JSON key, and keep the downloaded file private.

steps.title: Copy the service account fields into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the service account client email, private key ID, and private key. Keep the private key exactly as shown in the JSON file, including the BEGIN and END lines.

steps.title: Grant project permissions
steps.description: Make sure the service account has the Firebase or Google Cloud permissions needed for the projects and operations you will run.

name: Fireberry
description: Manage sales, marketing, service, and operations in one CRM.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use your Fireberry API token. It will be sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

setupGuide.title: Get your Fireberry API access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Fireberry API access uses a personal API access token. The token identifies the system user whose data and permissions the API will use.

steps.title: Open your Fireberry profile
steps.description: Sign in to Fireberry, click your profile picture in the top-right corner, and choose Profile.

steps.title: Open Account Security and then API Access Token
steps.description: In your profile, open the Account Security tab and then the API Access Token tab.

steps.title: Copy the token
steps.description: Copy the TokenID exactly as Fireberry shows it and store it securely.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud Fireberry connection form and paste the copied TokenID into the API key field.

actions.name: List Contacts
actions.description: Retrieves all contact records from Fireberry.

name: Firebolt
description: Run Firebolt queries and manage engines

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Authenticate Firebolt with a service account client ID and secret.

credentials.name: Account name
credentials.description: The Firebolt account name used to retrieve the system engine URL.

setupGuide.title: Set up Firebolt service account access
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Firebolt workspace and the target Firebolt account where this connection will run.

steps.title: Sign in to Firebolt
steps.description: Open the Firebolt workspace and sign in to the account you want to connect.

steps.title: Create a service account
steps.description: In Firebolt, open Configure > Service accounts, create a service account, and associate it with a user in the target account. Firebolt’s REST API docs require the service account to be associated with a user.

steps.title: Copy the service account ID
steps.description: In Configure > Service accounts, find the new service account and copy the value from the ID column.

steps.title: Generate and copy the service account secret
steps.description: From the same service account row, open the actions menu, choose Rotate secret, and copy the new secret immediately.

steps.title: Record the Firebolt account name
steps.description: Note the Firebolt account name from your authenticated workspace/account context. MindCloud uses it to call the documented engineUrl bootstrap endpoint for your account.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a FireHydrant API key with the raw token value sent in the Authorization header.
authentication.notes: FireHydrant API keys require Owner permissions. The raw token value is sent in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Connect FireHydrant
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need FireHydrant Owner permissions to create an API key.

steps.title: Open FireHydrant API Keys
steps.description: In FireHydrant, go to Settings and open API Keys.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click Create API key, enter a name and description, and save the key.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the token immediately and keep it somewhere safe. FireHydrant only shows the full token once.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud

name: Fiserv
description: Manage Fiserv payments, balances, transactions, payouts, and fees

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Fiserv Payments API requests with an API key in the x-api-key header.
authentication.notes: Fiserv Payments API docs require x-api-key header authentication. Use the private server-to-server API key; do not use the public JavaScript SDK key. The Linear ticket also lists Banking Hub host/token details, but this Stage 1 scaffold is anchored to the Payments API build block.

setupGuide.title: Connect Fiserv
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Fiserv says Payments API keys must be acquired from a sales representative. Use the private API key for server-to-server connections.

steps.title: Get a Fiserv Payments API private key
steps.description: Contact Fiserv sales or your Fiserv representative to acquire Payments API keys. Use the private key for this connection, not the public JavaScript SDK key.

steps.title: Enter the private API key in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the private API key into the API key field when creating the connection.

authentication.name: API Key and Secret
authentication.description: Authenticate Banking Hub token requests using HTTP Basic auth with the API key as username and API secret as password.
authentication.notes: Runtime evidence confirmed POST https://bankinghub-cert.fiservapis.com/fts-apim/oauth2/v2 with grant_type=client_credentials and HTTP Basic auth returns 200 OK with a bearer token. This Basic authentication now runs the Get Banking Hub Access Token action before protected API calls so the runtime can use credentials.custom.accessToken as a Bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Fiserv Banking Hub
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use the API key and API secret from Fiserv Developer Studio or the Linear credential handoff.

steps.title: Enter the API key
steps.description: Use the Fiserv API key as the username value.

steps.title: Enter the API secret
steps.description: Use the Fiserv API secret as the password value.

name: Fish Audio
description: Fish Audio is an AI voice generation platform for text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and custom voice model management.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Fish Audio API key. MindCloud sends it as a bearer token in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Connect Fish Audio
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Fish Audio account and an API key. MindCloud stores the key securely and sends it as a bearer token.

steps.title: Create or sign in to your Fish Audio account
steps.description: If you do not already have an account, sign up and complete any required verification.

steps.title: Open the API Keys page
steps.description: Go to the Fish Audio dashboard page for API keys.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click Create New Key, give it a descriptive name, and set an expiration if your team requires one.

steps.title: Copy the API key into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste the key into the API key field for this connection and save the connection.

steps.title: Validate the connection with a wallet read action
steps.description: Run the app connection test after saving. If Fish Audio reports missing credit, the connection can still be valid but paid-generation actions will remain blocked until the account is funded.

name: Fivetran
description: Fivetran is a managed data movement platform for programmatically managing accounts, destinations, connections, schemas, transformations, webhooks, and operational sync workflows through the Fivetran REST API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Provide your Fivetran API key and API secret. MindCloud sends them as HTTP Basic authentication using the documented api_key:api_secret format.

credentials.name: API Secret
credentials.description: The Fivetran API secret paired with the API key. Fivetran shows this value only when the secret is generated.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Fivetran API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Fivetran user or system API key with permissions for the account resources MindCloud should use.

steps.title: Open your Fivetran API key settings
steps.description: In the Fivetran dashboard, click your username, then click API Key.

steps.title: Generate or copy the key and secret
steps.description: Generate an API key if needed, then copy both the API key and API secret before leaving the page. Fivetran only shows the secret when it is generated.

steps.title: Paste the credentials into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API key into the API Key field and the API secret into the API Secret field.

name: Flexport
description: Flexport is a logistics platform for managing shipments, bookings, purchase orders, products, invoices, documents, customs data, and network resources through Flexport's public API.

authentication.name: OAuth2 Client Credentials
authentication.description: Use Flexport API Credentials (client ID and client secret) to obtain a bearer token for Flexport public API requests.
authentication.notes: Flexport uses OAuth2 client credentials for public API access. The token request uses client_id, client_secret, audience=https://api.flexport.com, and grant_type=client_credentials. Flexport endpoint access is controlled by resource selection on the API Credential rather than OAuth scope strings.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Flexport API Key bearer token for runtime verification and API access.
authentication.notes: Flexport API Keys are bearer tokens. Use this auth when testing whether API Keys unlock endpoints that return 403 with OAuth2 API Credentials. Requests should send Authorization: Bearer {{credentials.apiKey}} and Flexport-Version: 2023-07-01.

authentication.notes: Florm uses bearer-token authentication on the wire. Store the access token as the runtime source of truth. Keep the refresh token and tenant identifiers in the same secure credential envelope for continuity.

name: ForceManager
description: ForceManager (Sage Sales Management) REST API integration for CRM records such as companies, contacts, activities, opportunities, products, users, calendars, views, sales orders, and list-of-values resources.

authentication.name: Signed API Keys
authentication.description: ForceManager requires a support-issued public API key and private API key. Requests are authenticated with X-FM-PublicKey, X-FM-UnixTimestamp, and X-FM-Signature headers, where the signature is sha1(UnixTimestamp + APIPublicKey + APIPrivateKey).

credentials.name: Public API Key
credentials.description: Public API key issued by ForceManager support.

credentials.name: Private API Key
credentials.description: Private API key issued by ForceManager support. This is used to compute the X-FM-Signature header and must never be sent in plain text.

setupGuide.title: Set up ForceManager signed API keys
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active Sage Sales Management account and a public/private API key pair issued by ForceManager support.

steps.title: Confirm you have API access
steps.description: ForceManager documents that API use requires an active account plus a valid Public API Key and Private API Key.

steps.title: Request your API keys from ForceManager support
steps.description: Ask ForceManager support to issue a Public API Key and a Private API Key for this account.

steps.title: Enter the keys in this connection
steps.description: Paste the support-issued public key into Public API Key and the private key into Private API Key.

steps.title: Save the connection
steps.description: MindCloud will use the stored keys to build the ForceManager authentication headers X-FM-PublicKey, X-FM-UnixTimestamp, and X-FM-Signature for requests.

authentication.notes: Create an API key in Foreplay at https://app.foreplay.co/api-overview, then use that key when creating the connection. Foreplay's official docs send the key in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Connect Foreplay API
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Foreplay account with API access and permission to view the API dashboard.

steps.title: Open your Foreplay API settings
steps.description: In Foreplay, go to the API Overview page where Foreplay lets you create and copy your API key.

steps.title: Copy your API key
steps.description: Use the copy control in Foreplay to copy the API key shown on the API Overview page.

steps.title: Return to MindCloud and finish the connection
steps.description: Paste the copied value into the connection's API key field and save the connection.

name: Formbricks

setupGuide.title: Connect Formbricks with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Formbricks account and permission to create API keys in the environment you want to use.

steps.title: Sign in to Formbricks
steps.description: Open the hosted Formbricks app and sign in to the organization you want MindCloud to connect to.

steps.title: Open API key settings
steps.description: In the Formbricks app, go to Organization Settings > API Keys.

steps.title: Create and copy an API key
steps.description: Create a new API key, then copy the value immediately so you can paste it into MindCloud.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the copied value as the API Key when creating the Formbricks connection in MindCloud.

name: 123FormBuild
description: Build forms, collect data, and automate workflows

authentication.name: JWT Token
authentication.description: Use a 123FormBuilder JWT token generated from the API v2 authentication endpoint.

setupGuide.title: Get a 123FormBuilder JWT token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a 123FormBuilder account and either your username or email plus your password. If your account was created on the EU site, tell your MindCloud team before testing because the API uses a different base URL.

steps.title: Open the official Authentication docs
steps.description: Use the 123FormBuilder API v2 Authentication page. It documents the login, refresh, and invalidate token operations.

steps.title: Generate a token with the User login operation
steps.description: On that page, use the login endpoint to send your username or email and your password. The docs say you can also use passhash instead of a plain password if your account uses that flow.

steps.title: Paste the token into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Copy the returned token and paste it into the MindCloud connection field labeled API Key for this app.

name: Formspark
description: Formspark lets you send submissions to hosted form endpoints without running your own backend. This app wraps Formspark's documented public form submission surface, including AJAX submissions, redirect controls, feedback-page customization, reply routing, spam-protection fields, file-link submissions, and structured payload patterns.

name: Formstack
description: Build forms, collect submissions, and automate workflows

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Formstack with a Personal Access Token (PAT).

setupGuide.title: Connect Formstack with a Personal Access Token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Formstack account with access to the v2025 Forms API. If Personal Access Token creation is unavailable, ask your Organization Admin to enable PAT access for your user.

steps.title: Open the Formstack admin area
steps.description: Sign in to Formstack, go to the administration area, and open Access Tokens from the left-hand menu.

steps.title: Generate a new token
steps.description: Click Generate Token, then enter a unique name. You can also add an optional description and choose an expiration date of 30, 60, or 90 days.

steps.title: Copy the token immediately
steps.description: Copy the token string as soon as it is shown. Formstack displays the full token only once and it cannot be retrieved later.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud Formstack connection, use the API Key authentication method and paste the copied Personal Access Token into the API token field.

name: Fourthwall
description: Manage Fourthwall products, orders, promotions, and webhooks

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.scopes: shop_read offer_read offer_write order_read order_write fulfillment_write promotions_read promotions_write webhook_read webhook_write

setupGuide.title: Connect your Fourthwall shop
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Fourthwall shop admin account and a Fourthwall platform app for this connection.

steps.title: Open Platform apps in Fourthwall
steps.description: In your Fourthwall admin, open Platform apps and create a platform app or open the existing app you want to connect.

steps.title: Add the exact MindCloud redirect URL
steps.description: Under Advanced settings, add this redirect URL exactly: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/fourthwall/callback . Do not enter the Fourthwall /admin/platform-apps/.../connect URL here; that is the authorize URL, not the redirect URL.

steps.title: Select the required permissions
steps.description: Enable the permissions required by this wrapper: shop_read, offer_read, offer_write, order_read, order_write, fulfillment_write, promotions_read, promotions_write, webhook_read, and webhook_write.

steps.title: Confirm your app credentials
steps.description: Make sure you have the Client ID and Client Secret for this platform app available in MindCloud.

steps.title: Finish the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and start the connection. When Fourthwall opens the consent screen, approve the app to complete authentication.

name: Frameshift
description: Analyze genomic data and manage Mosaic projects, samples, and variants

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect with a Mosaic API bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Frameshift
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Frameshift Mosaic account with API access token credentials. The Stage 0 run stored the required values in the 1Password item named Frameshift.

steps.title: Open the API token settings page
steps.description: Sign in to Mosaic and open the page where API access tokens are created and listed.

steps.title: Create or locate an API access token
steps.description: Create a token if needed and capture the values shown by Frameshift. The Secret Access Token is only visible once when the token is created.

steps.title: Enter the bearer token in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the Secret Access Token into the API key field. Frameshift's API docs authenticate requests with an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

setupGuide.title: Connect FreeAgent
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a FreeAgent developer app so you can copy its Client ID and Client Secret into MindCloud.

steps.title: Create a FreeAgent developer app
steps.description: Open the FreeAgent Developer Dashboard and create an app to get your OAuth Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Add MindCloud as a redirect URI
steps.description: In your FreeAgent app settings, add the MindCloud OAuth redirect URI that the connection form shows you. FreeAgent requires the redirect URI to exactly match one registered in your Developer Dashboard account.

steps.title: Enter the app credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, paste the Client ID and Client Secret into the FreeAgent connection form and continue with the OAuth popup.

steps.title: Authorize the connection
steps.description: Sign in to FreeAgent in the popup window and approve the app so MindCloud receives an authorization code and exchanges it for access and refresh tokens.

name: FreshBooks
description: Manage clients, invoices, expenses, projects, and time entries

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: OAuth2 authorization code flow for FreshBooks APIs.
authentication.scopes: user:profile:read user:clients:read user:clients:write user:invoices:read user:invoices:write user:estimates:read user:estimates:write user:expenses:read user:expenses:write user:projects:read user:projects:write user:time_entries:read user:time_entries:write user:billable_items:read

setupGuide.title: Create FreshBooks OAuth credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Sign in to a FreshBooks account that can access the Developer Hub and make sure the FreshBooks app already includes the full scope set MindCloud will request for the FreshBooks build.

steps.title: Open the Developer Hub
steps.description: Open the FreshBooks Developer Hub and select Apps.

steps.title: Open the FreshBooks app you use for MindCloud
steps.description: Open the existing app whose Client ID and Client Secret you use in MindCloud.

steps.title: Confirm the full build scopes are enabled
steps.description: MindCloud now requests: user:profile:read, user:clients:read, user:clients:write, user:invoices:read, user:invoices:write, user:estimates:read, user:estimates:write, user:expenses:read, user:expenses:write, user:projects:read, user:projects:write, user:time_entries:read, user:time_entries:write, and user:billable_items:read. Make sure those same scopes are enabled on the FreshBooks app before you authorize.

steps.title: Re-authorize the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Start the FreshBooks authorization flow again so the access token is issued with the expanded scopes.

setupGuide.title: Connect Freshdesk API Key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Freshdesk account with API access enabled for your user.

steps.title: Find your Freshdesk subdomain and API key
steps.description: In Freshdesk, open Profile settings and copy your API key. Your subdomain is the part before .freshdesk.com in your helpdesk URL.

steps.title: Enter credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Set Subdomain to your tenant slug (for example mindcloud). Use your Freshdesk API key as username and X as password in the Basic auth fields.

name: Freshsales Classic
description: Freshsales Classic is a Freshworks CRM integration for managing contacts, accounts, deals, tasks, search, and related sales data through the legacy Freshsales API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use your Freshsales Classic CRM API key together with your Freshworks CRM bundle alias.

credentials.name: Bundle Alias
credentials.description: Your Freshworks CRM bundle alias, for example yourcompany.myfreshworks.com/crm/sales.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Freshsales Classic account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to your Freshworks CRM account settings so you can copy your API key and bundle alias.

steps.title: Open your Freshworks CRM profile settings
steps.description: In Freshworks CRM, click your profile picture and choose Profile Settings.

steps.title: Open the API Settings tab
steps.description: Select the API Settings tab inside Profile Settings.

steps.title: Copy your API key
steps.description: Copy the value shown in the Your API key field.

steps.title: Copy your bundle alias
steps.description: Copy the bundle alias shown below your API key. It looks like yourcompany.myfreshworks.com/crm/sales.

steps.title: Paste both values into MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the API key into the API Key field and the bundle alias into the Bundle Alias field.
